neighbours.label: nouns for a person sent to carry word on someone's behalf: emissary, envoy, messenger, herald, courier (and Arabic رسول, weaker in other languages); postman, prophet, angel, diplomat and the word 'message' stay quiet
fire: The king sent an emissary across the mountains to negotiate a truce.
A royal herald rode into the square and read the proclamation aloud.
The courier arrived at dawn with a sealed letter for the general.
She served as the envoy of the republic at the peace talks in Vienna.
Breathless, the messenger fell to his knees before the queen.
The rebels dispatched an envoy to meet the governor in secret.
Every morning a courier from the bank picked up the signed documents.
Don't shoot the messenger; I'm only telling you what the board decided.
quiet: The king wrote a letter across the mountains to negotiate a truce.
A royal decree was posted in the square and read aloud by the crowd.
The postman arrived at dawn with a sealed letter for the general.
She served as a diplomat of the republic at the peace talks in Vienna.
Breathless, the soldier fell to his knees before the queen.
The rebels sent a message to the governor in secret.
Every morning the bank's manager signed the documents himself.
Don't blame me; I'm only telling you what the board decided.
